From: Elena Park <elena@cloudmed.ai>
To: jonas@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: CloudMed dedicated ask — traffic profile and SLOs

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this. We are preparing to move a production feature (patient chart summarization) to Redwood Dedicated and need a focused sizing recommendation. High-level traffic and SLOs below: 

- Typical window: daily 11:30 - 14:30 PST (peak hours)
- Baseline: ~25 requests/sec; average prompt+response ~120 tokens per request
- Bursts: up to ~80 requests/sec for short spikes (2–4 minutes), observed ~2x per day
- Quality requirement: current LLM baseline matches our clinical prompts; we prefer not to degrade quality below current model (we'll call this "cloudmed-prod-13b")
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 350ms for user-facing summarization (we can tolerate occasional p99 spikes)

I attached a small token profile export (CloudMed_token_profile.csv) with per-endpoint request mix. Primary asks: 
1) What dedicated slab (GPU count/type) would you recommend for committed capacity to meet p95 <= 350ms with reasonable headroom?
2) How much burst capacity would you advise to keep on-call risk low?
3) Any suggested fallback model variants and automated routing policies to maintain SLOs during contention?

Can we get a short write-up this week so we can present to our infra committee?

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Park
Head of Platform
CloudMed Health

(attachment: CloudMed_token_profile.csv)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@cloudmed.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-02T12:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: CloudMed dedicated ask — traffic profile and SLOs

Elena — thanks, received the token profile and the traffic mix. Quick summary/first pass below; Priyom and Marissa copied for sizing and pricing follow-up.

Short answers up front:
- Baseline tokens/sec (median window): ~3,000 tok/s (25 rps * 120 tok)
- Burst requirement: ~9,600 tok/s (80 rps * 120 tok)
- Recommended committed slab: 2 GPUs (primary) + 1 hot-standby for burst/rotation; see Priyom's model-level numbers for actual per-GPU throughput.

Notes / rationale:
- We want at least 50% headroom on committed capacity to keep p95 comfortable and allow for background KV/cache warmups. That pushes baseline target to ~4,500 tok/s.
- For safety during regular bursts, we recommend a burst pool that can add the equivalent of 1–2 additional GPUs quickly (auto-scaling/burst credit).
- Fallback policy: route to a slightly smaller model variant (7B-int8-ish) under sustained pressure; this preserves p95 but will require a QA check on quality regressions for your clinical prompts.

Priyom — can you drop the per-model tok/s numbers and the quick slab calc? Marissa — I'll let you handle commit options after Priyom's calc.

Best,
Jonas
Director, Solutions (Redwood Inference)

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Elena Park <elena@cloudmed.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-03T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: CloudMed dedicated ask — traffic profile and SLOs (model-level calc)

Elena / team — I ran a short model-level throughput and latency map using the token profile you shared. Attached is the slab calc workbook (redwood_gpu_slab_calc.xlsx); key excerpts below. All measurements are approximate and assume 8k context offload for longer histories.

Per-GPU sustained tokens/sec (approx, production-optimized kernels):
- redwood-13B-quant (13B, q4_k_mixed): ~2,800 tok/s per A100-like GPU (good quality, higher memory footprint)
- redwood-7B-int8 (7B, int8-opt): ~5,200 tok/s per A100-like GPU (faster, slightly lower quality on edge cases)
- redwood-3B-fast (3B, int8): ~9,800 tok/s per GPU (low latency, moderate quality dip)

Requested targets and mapping:
- Baseline need: 3,000 tok/s -> with 13B-quant you'd need 2 GPUs (2 * 2,800 = 5,600 tok/s, ~87% util -> reasonable but tight if background tasks run)
- Target with 50% headroom: 4,500 tok/s -> 2 GPUs on 13B gives enough headroom; 1 GPU on 7B-int8 would also satisfy baseline headroom (5,200 tok/s) but quality delta must be validated
- Burst cover to 9,600 tok/s -> requires either 2 GPUs on 7B-int8 (10.4k tok/s) or add a hot standby GPU (so 3 GPUs total: 2 committed + 1 burst).

Latency implications (empirical):
- redwood-13B-quant at 60–80% GPU utilization: p50 ~80–120ms, p95 ~280–350ms, p99 ~450–700ms (depends on sequence length distribution)
- redwood-7B-int8 at equivalent utilization: p50 ~50–70ms, p95 ~150–220ms, p99 ~300–420ms

Recommendation (practical):
1) Commit to a 2-GPU dedicated slab sized for redwood-13B-quant. This meets baseline + ~50% headroom and keeps model quality.
2) Add a 1-GPU hot-standby/burst credit to handle the 2–4 minute spikes. This can be invoked via our burst pool routing policy; warm cache policy recommended to avoid cold-start penalties.
3) Configure an automated fallback to redwood-7B-int8 when queuing latency or memory pressure is detected; include a weighted rollout to validate quality under traffic.

I've attached the calc workbook and a short CSV with per-endpoint token splits. Let me know if you want the same numbers on a different GPU profile (e.g., A10 vs A100) — that will change per-GPU tok/s by ~15–30%.

(attachment: redwood_gpu_slab_calc.xlsx)

— Priyom
Senior Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
